tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session opens http://localhost:8000/?page_id=2, analyses the page repeatedly to locate the 'Sample Page' nav link, records a stable href-based selector (a[href$='?page_id=2']) and a deterministic elementHash 'ca1241e345', and then clicks the nav link to verify the H1 and URL. Click attempts in the session did not produce navigation because the current page was already the target URL; the tool must still demonstrate the nav click and verify the page state.

Task Definition:
- Provide a reusable automation tool that: 1) navigates to a starting URL containing site navigation, 2) verifies the presence and visibility of the top navigation 'Sample Page' link, 3) clicks that link (using the recorded elementHash when available), and 4) extracts the page H1 and URL to confirm the static informational page has been opened/read.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to the composed start URL: {base_url}/?page_id={page_id}.
2) Extract page content and list interactive elements to confirm the nav link candidate and H1 presence (output: initial_page). This allows runtime verification before interaction.
3) Click the target nav anchor. Prefer deterministic elementHash 'ca1241e345' (recorded from the session). If the elementHash is not available or invalid in a new environment, fall back to CSS selector a[href$='?page_id={page_id}'] or use {nav_selector} if provided.
4) Re-extract page content (output: final_page) and verify main heading (h1) text and that the URL contains 'page_id={page_id}'. Return both extracted outputs for audit and assertions.

Variable Identification:
- base_url (required): the site base URL (scheme + host + optional port). Derived from the recorded navigation 'http://localhost:8000'.
- page_id (required): the numeric identifier used in the navigation link query parameter; recorded value '2'.
- h1_text (optional): expected H1 text to assert the correct page was opened; recorded example 'Sample Page'.
- nav_selector (optional): an alternative CSS selector to scope the nav link (useful in environments where href or host differs).
- nav_elementHash (optional): the recorded elementHash 'ca1241e345' for deterministic click targeting. If provided, it will be used in the click step.

Step Optimization:
- Navigation is implemented as a direct URL navigation to {base_url}/?page_id={page_id} (deterministic and faster). Although the recorded session repeatedly re-analysed the page and attempted clicks (sometimes redundant because the current page already matched the nav target), we still perform the click to demonstrate navigation via site controls as required.
- Use the recorded elementHash 'ca1241e345' for deterministic clicking where possible. Also include an href-suffix CSS selector (a[href$='?page_id={page_id}']) which is stable across host changes and can be scoped using {nav_selector}.
- Runtime visibility checks (presence, computed-style visibility, bounding box, elementFromPoint occlusion checks) are recommended and captured by the extract_page_content steps so test harnesses can implement them prior to click. These checks were emphasized in the recorded session and must be executed by the runner (not by this static definition) to avoid flaky interactions.
- Avoid optional exploratory steps: the tool focuses only on the required actions (open page, verify nav link, click nav link, confirm H1/URL). It does not include unrelated filtering, sorting, or additional navigation.

Edge cases & Notes:
- If the starting page already equals the target (same URL), clicking may be a no-op or reload. The tool still performs the click to demonstrate using the nav link; the final_page extraction will validate the H1 & URL in either case.
- If the elementHash is stale in a different environment, the click step's cssSelector will be used. If multiple matches exist, the runner should scope the selector to header/nav (e.g., nav a[href*='page_id={page_id}']) or filter by visible text.
- The agent is assumed to be already authenticated when required; no auth steps are included.

Deterministic behavior & required inputs:
- The tool is deterministic: navigation uses input parameters, click targets the recorded elementHash or a stable href-based selector, and extraction steps return reproducible H1 and URL data. Inputs required: base_url and page_id. Optional inputs allow robustness across environments.

This analysis establishes the minimal, deterministic, and reusable steps required to replicate the recorded browser sequence for opening and reading the Sample Page via site navigation.
name: open_and_read_sample_page_via_nav
description: Open the site starting URL, locate and click the top-navigation 'Sample Page' link, then confirm the page was opened by extracting the H1 heading and verifying the URL. Uses the recorded elementHash 'ca1241e345' for a deterministic click; falls back to href-based selector when needed.

steps.description: Navigate to the starting URL that should contain the top navigation with the 'Sample Page' link.
Capture page title, available links and a candidate selector for the 'Sample Page' nav link so runtime checks can be performed.
steps.goal: List interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs), confirm presence of navigation link to '?page_id={page_id}', and confirm H1 existence before performing the nav click.

steps.description: Deterministically click the top-navigation 'Sample Page' link. Uses recorded elementHash 'ca1241e345' when available; otherwise uses a href-suffix selector scoped by {nav_selector} if provided, else a[href$='?page_id={page_id}'].
Verify the static informational page was opened and read by extracting the H1 and page URL.
steps.goal: After clicking the navigation link, confirm the resulting page by extracting the main H1 text and current URL; report whether the URL contains 'page_id={page_id}' and whether the H1 matches {h1_text} (if provided).

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base site URL (scheme + host + optional port). Example: "http://localhost:8000"

input_schema.name: page_id
input_schema.description: Numeric page identifier used in the navigation link query parameter (the tool will target '?page_id={page_id}'). Example: "2"

input_schema.name: h1_text
input_schema.description: Expected H1 text on the target page to verify the page loaded. If omitted the tool will still extract and return the H1 found. Example: "Sample Page"

input_schema.name: nav_selector
input_schema.description: Optional CSS selector to scope the navigation link. If provided it will be used instead of the default href-suffix selector. Example: "nav a[href$='?page_id={page_id}']"

input_schema.name: nav_elementHash
input_schema.description: Optional elementHash for a deterministic click. Recorded elementHash from the session: "ca1241e345". If provided it will be preferred for the click action.
